o: Group the letters of s by their exact frequency. Among these frequency groups, pick the one containing the most distinct characters; break size ties by choosing the larger frequency k. Return that group's characters in any order.
k: Bucket characters by count; the answer is the bucket with maximum cardinality.
Ties in cardinality resolve to the higher frequency key.
At most 26 distinct letters, so everything is tiny.

a.i: Count each character's occurrences, invert the map into frequency → character list, then select the list maximizing (size, frequency) lexicographically. Joining the winners gives the answer.
s: Invert into groups keyed by frequency.
a.t: O(n + 26²) — counting plus a scan over at most 26 frequency groups

w: Straightforward counting; the only trap is the tie rule — compare group sizes first, then frequencies (Example 3 picks frequency 2 over frequency 1 despite equal sizes). Any order of output characters is accepted.
